extracted.intended_audience: K–12 mathematics teachers, curriculum designers, and assessment developers
extracted.subtask_description: A rubric for judging the quality of K–12 mathematical work (homework, projects, classroom performance, assessment items, or answers) based on five process standards describing mathematical practice. Emphasizes problem solving, reasoning/proof, communication, connections, and representation across grades K–12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem Solving
rubrics_metrics.description: Building new mathematical knowledge through problem solving (not just exercising known knowledge). Solving problems that arise in mathematics and in other contexts. Applying and adapting a variety of strategies — generalize, specialize, work backward, draw a figure, look for symmetry. Monitoring and reflecting on the process — metacognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visible signal: Multiple strategies considered; reflection at the end. A good performance demonstrates generating and using diverse strategies and reflecting on the approach and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoning and Proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize reasoning and proof as fundamental aspects of mathematics. Make and investigate mathematical conjectures. Develop and evaluate mathematical arguments and proofs. Select and use various types of reasoning and methods of proof — direct, contrapositive, contradiction, induction, case analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visible signal: Conjecture stated; argument follows; method named. Emphasize making conjectures, justifying claims, and choosing/identifying proof methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize and consolidate thinking through communication. Communicate coherently and clearly to peers, teachers, others. Analyze and evaluate the thinking and strategies of others. Use the language of mathematics to express ideas precisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visible signal: Complete sentences; clear notation; precise vocabulary. Assess clarity of exposition, correctness and consistency of notation, and ability to explain and critique reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and use connections among mathematical ideas. See mathematics as a coherent whole, not a list of disconnected procedures. Recognize and apply mathematics in contexts outside of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visible signal: Reference to related results; placement in larger picture. Look for links to prior topics, other domains, or real-world contexts that show coherent understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Create and use representations to organize, record, and communicate ideas. Select, apply, and translate among multiple representations (algebraic, geometric, graphical, tabular, verbal). Use representations to model and interpret physical, social, and mathematical phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visible signal: At least two of: algebra, picture, table, graph, words. Evaluate the appropriateness, accuracy, and translation between representations and their use for modeling/interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCTM's implicit rubric for evaluating a math performance
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete piece of mathematical work — a homework solution, a project, a Q&A answer — should exhibit all five processes (Problem Solving; Reasoning and Proof; Communication; Connections; Representation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the five processes together as an integrated checklist: look for multiple strategies and reflection (problem solving), explicit conjectures and structured arguments (reasoning/proof), clear language and notation (communication), references to related ideas (connections), and multiple representations (representation). The table of visible signals maps each process to observable indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Core Standards for Mathematical Practice (SMPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eight practices that extend NCTM's processes: (1) Make sense of problems and persevere. (2) Reason abstractly and quantitatively. (3) Construct viable arguments and critique others. (4) Model with mathematics. (5) Use appropriate tools strategically. (6) Attend to precision. (7) Look for and make use of structure. (8) Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These SMPs are explicit descendants of NCTM's processes and can be used as criteria when evaluating student work or designing instruction and assessment. Note emphasis on precision (careful notation, units, definitions) and on modeling, tool use, structure, and repeated reasoning.
